title: Topological fibres and invariant closed images of an affine PGL quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\geq2$, and $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$, the group scheme of [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover]. Let $E$ be a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra and $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with an action of $G$ by $k$-scheme morphisms satisfying the group laws. Write $\rho:E\to E\otimes_k k[G]$ for its coordinate coaction and $E^G=\ker(\rho-(e\mapsto e\otimes1))$. Then the invariant algebra is finitely generated and the map $p:U\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)$ is surjective. For every invariant closed subset $D\subseteq U$, its image $p(D)$ is closed in $Y$. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ and every $y\in Y(\Omega)$, the geometric fibre $U_y$ contains a unique $G_\Omega$-orbit closed in $U_y$; the closure in $U_y$ of every orbit contains this closed orbit. For every field extension $K/k$, the canonical map $K\otimes_k E^G\to(K\otimes_k E)^{G_K}$ is an isomorphism, identifying the invariant quotient after extension with $p_K:U_K\to Y_K$. For every invariant closed subset $D$ as above, the image of its inverse image $D_K\subseteq U_K$ under $p_K$ is the inverse image of $p(D)$ in $Y_K$, as subsets. These assertions permit nonreduced $U$ and nonreduced stabilizers and impose no characteristic restriction.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, arXiv:1005.2398v3, Theorem 9.1.4 and Remark 9.1.5 (affine quotient), Theorem 9.7.6 (reductive implies geometrically reductive), Theorem 5.3.1(1)--(5) (surjectivity, invariant closed images, orbit-closure equivalence), Theorem 6.3.3 (finite generation), Proposition 5.2.9 (flat base change). Unique closed orbit is the orbit-closure formulation of 5.3.1 combined with the orbit lemma; the field-extension invariant equality is the flat equalizer calculation. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $A=E^G$. The PGL power-lifting theorem gives finite generation of $A$ and the power-lifting hypothesis for all finite-type equivariant algebra quotients. The affine action-stack presentation applies because PGL is smooth affine of finite type. The adequate-affine-quotient criterion therefore makes $\phi:[U/G]\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ an adequate moduli space, and its composite with the smooth surjective atlas $q:U\to[U/G]$ is exactly $p$. Adequate-moduli surjectivity and atlas surjectivity give surjectivity of $p$.

source.place: Theorem 9.1.4, Remark 9.1.5, Theorem 5.3.1(1); assembly from existing finite-type power-lifting criterion.

proof.text: For a field extension $K/k$, tensor the exact sequence $0\to A\to E\xrightarrow{\rho-(-\otimes1)}E\otimes_k k[G]$ with the flat $k$-module $K$. Flat tensor exactness identifies its first term with the kernel of the extended difference map. Under the canonical tensor associativity identifications that map is precisely the coaction difference for $G_K$ on $K\otimes_kE$. Thus the canonical map $K\otimes_kA\to(K\otimes_kE)^{G_K}$ is bijective; it respects multiplication since both sides are subalgebras of $K\otimes_kE$. Its inclusion into $K\otimes_kE$ is the tensor of $A\hookrightarrow E$, so the associated affine quotient is $p_K$. The matrix central-cover description identifies $G_K$ with $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,K}$. Consequently Step 1 applies over every such $K$.

source.place: Flat tensor preserves kernels: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), (2) implies (1), with Tag 00HB (definition-flat); explicit coaction equalizer. No exactness of the invariant functor is asserted.

proof.text: For an invariant closed subset $D\subseteq U$, the two inverse images under $a,\operatorname{pr}_2:G\times U\rightrightarrows U$ agree. By the presentation-topology theorem it is $q^{-1}(C)$ for a closed subset $C\subseteq|[U/G]|$, and $C$ has a reduced closed substack structure. Adequate-moduli closedness gives $p(D)=\phi(C)$ closed. Moreover, for invariant closed $D_1,D_2$, their corresponding closed substacks satisfy $p(D_1)\cap p(D_2)=p(D_1\cap D_2)$: apply the intersection-of-images assertion and pull back the intersection to the atlas. This argument works over every extension field by Step 2 and Step 1.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(2),(4); stacks-properties.tex Tags 04XJ, 04XL, 0509 for passage through the presentation.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ and $y\in Y(\Omega)$. Steps 1--2 give a nonempty fibre $F=U_y=\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_A\Omega)$. The images of finitely many $k$-algebra generators of $E$ generate $E\otimes_A\Omega$ over $\Omega$, so $F$ is affine finite type. The $\Omega$-algebra map $\Omega\otimes_kA\to\Omega$ defining $y$ is surjective because it contains the constants; its kernel is maximal. Thus $y$ is closed in $Y_\Omega$ and $F$ is closed in $U_\Omega$, as required in Step 5. A nonempty closed subset of an affine scheme has a closed point by the quasi-compact Kolmogorov closed-point lemma, and the finite-type closed-point residue-field theorem makes that point $\Omega$-rational. This applies also to every nonempty closed subset of $F$, with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure. The group $G_\Omega$ is smooth connected affine of finite type by the matrix-cover theorem. Apply the smooth-group orbit lemma to its action on $F$: orbits are locally closed, their closures and boundaries are invariant, and all boundary orbits have strictly smaller dimension. First choose a rational point of $F$ by the closed-point argument, so rational-point orbits exist. In the closure of any such orbit choose a rational-point orbit of minimum dimension, possible since the set contains the original orbit and its dimensions are nonnegative integers. Its boundary is closed in its closure because the orbit is locally closed; its closure lies in the original orbit closure by minimality of topological closure. If this boundary were nonempty, it would contain a rational point by the preceding closed-point argument, whose orbit has smaller dimension. Hence this minimum orbit is closed in $F$.

source.place: Propositions 7.4--7.6 (orbit boundaries), combined with the closed-point argument (Stacks Tags 005E, 01TB, 01J3). Local Milne PDF WANTED; assembly argument by worker.

proof.text: Let $O_x,O_z$ be closed orbits in $F$ of $x,z\in F(\Omega)$. By the orbit lemma their closures, i.e. themselves, are invariant, so they are invariant closed subsets of $U_\Omega$ since $F=p_\Omega^{-1}(y)$ is closed. Suppose $O_x\cap O_z\neq\emptyset$. This closed subset of the affine scheme $F$ contains a closed point $w$ by the Kolmogorov closed-point lemma, and $w$ is $\Omega$-rational by the closed-point residue-field theorem. The fibre of the orbit map $G_\Omega\to O_x$, $g\mapsto gx$, over $w$ is a nonempty closed subscheme of the affine finite-type scheme $G_\Omega$ (the orbit lemma gives surjectivity), so by the same two lemmas it has a rational point $g$ with $gx=w$; likewise $hz=w$ with $h\in G(\Omega)$. Right translations being automorphisms of $G_\Omega$, $O_x=O_w=O_z$. Hence distinct closed orbits are disjoint, whereas Step 3 over $\Omega$ makes the intersection of their images equal to the image of their intersection; both images are $\{y\}$ and the image of $\emptyset$ is empty, a contradiction. Thus $F$ has a unique closed orbit. Step 4 applied inside each orbit closure gives an orbit closed in $F$ inside it, which is therefore this unique one. Hence every orbit closure contains it.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(4); uniqueness argument using Steps 3--4, with disjointness of distinct orbits from the closed-point lemmas.

proof.text: Finally give $D$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $D_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U$. Its pullback to $U_K$ has underlying subset exactly $D_K$, irrespective of whether that pullback is reduced. Apply the set-theoretic image/base-change assertion for 2-fibre products to the scheme map $D_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$ and $Y_K\to Y$: the image of $D_{\mathrm{red}}\times_YY_K=D_{\mathrm{red}}\times_kK$ is precisely the inverse image of $p(D)$ in $Y_K$. By Step 2 its map to $Y_K$ is the restriction of $p_K$, proving the last assertion. Every preceding input permits nonreduced schemes and nonreduced stabilizers; none requires an inverse to the characteristic or to $r$.

source.place: Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), specialized to schemes; Tag 01J3 (schemes.tex, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme).
